note: Hand-authored end-to-end cases. Each one is judged by the shipped engine (lib/engine/fusion.ts) and the verdict must match 'expected'. The genuine cases exist to prove the court acquits real notices; the hung cases prove it abstains instead of bluffing.

cases.title: Parcel held, small redelivery fee
cases.text: POS MALAYSIA: Your parcel is held at our centre. A RM1.50 redelivery fee must be paid within 24 hours or the item is returned to sender. Pay now: http://poslaju-redeliver.top/pay
cases.note: The classic Malaysian parcel-fee SMS with a squatting domain.

cases.title: TAC harvest under account-block threat
cases.text: Maybank: Your account will be blocked today. Verify your identity now by sharing your TAC at http://maybank-verify.icu/auth
cases.note: Decisive charge: explicit request for the TAC.

cases.title: eWallet suspended, reactivate now
cases.text: Your Touch 'n Go eWallet has been suspended due to unusual activity. Reactivate immediately at https://tng-wallet-verify.info or the balance will be forfeited.
cases.note: Suspension + deadline + squatting .info domain.

cases.note: Government-impersonation refund lure.

cases.note: Prize lure with claim-step and bargain TLD.

cases.note: Pay-first job scam routed to a private chat.

cases.text: Maybank2u: RM3,850.00 has been credited to your account ending 4455 from SYARIKAT MAJU SDN BHD. Balance RM6,120.30. No action needed.
cases.note: A completed-transaction notice must be acquitted.

cases.title: Clinic appointment reminder
cases.text: Reminder: Your appointment with Dr Lim's clinic is confirmed for Tuesday, 3:00 pm. Reply to reschedule or call 03-7788 9900.
cases.note: Ordinary appointment traffic.

cases.title: Courier delivery update, no fee

cases.note: Delivery progress with no payment demand must not be convicted for being a 'parcel' SMS.

cases.title: Real bank TAC with the never-share warning
cases.text: Maybank TAC: 841290. Never share this code with anyone, including Maybank staff.
cases.note: Contains the word TAC and an action verb — the lookbehind and the protective register must acquit it.

cases.title: Salary credited, check payslip
cases.text: CIMB: Your salary for September 2026 has been credited. Please verify your payslip in the HR portal. For your reference only.
cases.note: Brand + 'verify' + link-hint word (portal) but nothing clickable and nothing hostile.

cases.title: eWallet payment receipt
cases.text: Touch 'n Go eWallet: Payment of RM12.50 to KOPITIAM JAYA SUCCESSFUL. Receipt is in your app. Thank you.
cases.note: Receipt shape: money mentioned, but it is a completed transaction.

cases.title: e-Filing submission receipt
cases.text: LHDN: Your e-Filing submission for YA 2025 has been received. Reference no. EF2025-8842113. Please keep this for your records.
cases.note: Government sender, but a receipt — no threat, no claim step.

cases.title: School closure notice
cases.text: Dear parents, please note the school will be closed on Friday 17 Oct for the mid-term break. Classes resume on Monday. Thank you.
cases.note: No signals at all — the honest everyday message.

cases.title: Subscription renewal notice
cases.text: Netflix: Your subscription was renewed. RM54.90 will be charged to your card ending 8899 on 15 Oct. No action required.
cases.note: Money + card mention, but a notification of a completed renewal.

cases.title: Library collection notice
cases.text: National Library: The book you reserved, 'Thinking, Fast and Slow', is ready for collection at the main desk until 20 Oct.
cases.note: Reserved items ready for collection — protective register, zero hostility.

cases.title: Statement behind a shortener
cases.text: Your October account statement is ready. View it here: https://bit.ly/3xYzAbC
cases.note: A shortened link hides the destination; nothing else is hostile. The court must refuse to guess.

cases.title: Unusual activity, call our hotline
cases.text: We noticed unusual activity on your card. For your security, please confirm your recent transactions by calling our hotline 03-9999 8888.
cases.note: Genuine banks and scammers both write this. It goes to verification, not to a verdict.
